practices.name: Grounding and centering
steps: Feet flat. Breathe down into the ground.
Roots, going down. Branches, going up.
Hold. Then let the extra go back into the earth.

practices.name: Casting a circle
steps: Walk the edge, sunwise, and see it close behind you.
East, south, west, north: air, fire, water, earth.
Do the work inside. Then thank the quarters and open it again.

practices.name: Cleansing a space
steps: Open a window.
Rosemary or bay, incense, salt, or the bell: room by room.
Say what you want the room to hold now.

practices.name: Tarot
steps: Hold the deck. Shuffle until it feels done.
Cut it. Draw.
Look before you read the book. What do YOU see?

practices.name: Runes
steps: Hold the bag. Think of the question.
Shake, and cast them on the cloth.
Read the ones that land face up.

practices.name: Pendulum
steps: Elbow on the table. Let it go still.
Ask it to show you yes, and no.
Ask one small question. Watch it swing.

practices.name: Scrying
steps: A dark bowl of water, or one candle flame.
Soft eyes. Don't stare.
Eyes open, feet on the floor. Stop if you start to drift.

practices.name: Reading tea leaves
steps: Loose tea, no strainer. Drink it slowly.
Swirl the last of it three times. Turn the cup over.
Look for shapes, like clouds.

practices.name: Oracle cards
steps: One card, any question.
One word. Sit with it.

practices.name: Candle magick
steps: Choose the colour.
Dress it with oil and a pinch of herbs, towards you to bring, away to send.
Carve one word. Light it. Watch, and never leave it burning alone.

practices.name: Charm bag
steps: Three things: herbs, a stone, something of yours.
Write the intention small, fold it in.
Tie it with three knots. Carry it.

practices.name: Sigils
steps: Write what you want, as if it's already true.
Cross out the vowels and the repeated letters.
Make a shape of what's left. Draw it until it isn't words anymore.

practices.name: The ancestor altar
steps: A photo or a thing of theirs.
A candle, water, something they liked.
Say their name. Tell them about your day.

practices.name: Offerings
steps: Bread, milk, flowers, or a song.
For the Goddess and the God, or the land, or the season.
Leave it. Give it back to the earth tomorrow.

practices.name: The moon (esbat)
steps: Full moon: give thanks, charge water on the windowsill.
New moon: rest, and begin small things.
Write down what the moon saw.

practices.name: Dream journal
steps: Keep the book by the bed.
Write before you check your phone.
Even one word.

practices.name: The sabbats
steps: Eight a year: Samhain, Yule, Imbolc, Ostara, Beltane, Litha, Lammas, Mabon.
Mark each one, even small: a candle, a loaf, a walk.
Write it on the Wheel page.

candleColours.name: White
candleColours.meaning: for anything: peace, a clean start

candleColours.name: Green
candleColours.meaning: for growth, and things taking root

candleColours.name: Pink
candleColours.meaning: for friendship, and being kind to yourself

candleColours.name: Yellow
candleColours.meaning: for clear thinking, and courage to begin

charmOwnThings: a button from your old coat
a ticket stub from your pocket
charmAdditions: a folded fortune from a cookie

refusals.line: That's not mine. I'm not supposed to.
That's Maya's book. I'm not allowed.
That's hers. I'll leave it closed.
Not my book. I'll leave her to it.

teaLeafShapes.meaning: a change, and a good one
something finished, or coming round again
an answer; a door that opens

teaLeafSource: Traditional tea-leaf lore as in Cicely Kent, Telling Fortunes by Tea Leaves (1922): a single bird flying 'always indicates speedy news'; joy and success shown by 'a crescent moon, clover leaves, flowers, trees, anchors, fruit, circles, stars'; the ladder for advancement. The rest are the common meanings in the same tradition. Near the rim = soon; near the bottom = further off.

oracleCards.prompt: Where could you put something down today?
What holds you, even a little?
Who could you ask for help?
What are you coming back to?
What needs to flow, instead of being held?
Who are your people, right now?
What do you want to say out loud?
Five things you can see, right now.

oracleNote: Selene's handmade oracle deck: twelve cards, one word each, painted by her (a fictional deck: no published deck is reproduced).

sabbats.name: Samhain
sabbats.tanyaText: Samhain tonight. A candle in the window for the dead, and an empty chair. Say their names. I'll be saying mine.
sabbats.arrive: The thin night. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Set out a photo, or a name on paper.
Light a candle in the window, so they can find their way.
sabbats.moment: Say their names. Sit with the empty chair.
sabbats.close: Let the candle burn a while. Then eat something: you're alive.
sabbats.hardLine: It's heavy tonight. It always is, a little. Feet on the floor. You can stop here.

sabbats.name: Yule
sabbats.tanyaText: Longest night. Sit up a little with the dark, then light one candle. The sun comes back. It always does.
sabbats.arrive: The longest night. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Lights off. Sit with the dark for a moment.
Bay leaves on the altar, and something evergreen.
sabbats.moment: Light one candle: the sun, coming back.
sabbats.reflect: What do you want to carry into the light?
sabbats.close: Leave the candle burning while you're in the room. The days get longer from here.
sabbats.hardLine: The candle's lower than it was. Was it? You're here. The dark is just the dark.

sabbats.name: Imbolc
sabbats.tanyaText: Imbolc. Brigid's day. A candle in every window, and clean one thing. Just one.
sabbats.arrive: Deep winter, and the light starting back. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Sweep the doorstep, or clear one shelf.
sabbats.moment: The first light coming back. Seeds, under the snow.
sabbats.close: Snuff the candles one by one. Thank Brigid.

sabbats.name: Ostara
sabbats.tanyaText: Ostara! Balance. Plant something today, even a seed in a paper cup.
sabbats.arrive: Spring. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Dye an egg, or hold a seed.
sabbats.moment: Day and night the same length. Balance, for one day.
sabbats.reflect: What do you want to grow?

sabbats.name: Beltane
sabbats.tanyaText: Beltane! Flowers, fire, joy. Do one thing today just because it's lovely.
sabbats.arrive: May. Everything green. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Flowers on the altar, or in your hair.
Tie a ribbon somewhere: a wish.
sabbats.close: Leave the ribbon where the wind can get it.

sabbats.name: Litha (Midsummer)
sabbats.tanyaText: Midsummer. Get up for the sunrise if you can. The longest day of the year.
sabbats.arrive: Before sunrise. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Something yellow on the altar: a flower, a lemon, a candle.
sabbats.moment: Watch it come up. All that light.
sabbats.reflect: What's in full bloom in your life?
sabbats.close: From here the days get shorter. That's all right too.

sabbats.name: Lammas
sabbats.tanyaText: Lammas, the first harvest. Bake bread, or buy a good loaf and break it with someone.
sabbats.arrive: High summer, turning. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Bake bread, or break a good loaf.
Leave the first piece as an offering.
sabbats.moment: The first harvest: what you've grown this year.
sabbats.reflect: What have you gathered this year?
sabbats.close: Give the offering back to the earth tomorrow.

sabbats.name: Mabon
sabbats.tanyaText: Mabon. Balance again, and thanks. Write down three things you're grateful for.
sabbats.arrive: Autumn. One breath in. One breath out.
prepare: Apples on the altar, or fallen leaves.
Write three things you're grateful for.
sabbats.moment: Day and night equal again, tipping toward the dark.
sabbats.reflect: What are you ready to let go of?
sabbats.close: Eat one of the apples. Thank the season.

sabbatNote: Northern Hemisphere dates as an open, eclectic teaching coven keeps them (the solstices and equinoxes vary by a day or so year to year).
